awd_titl_txt: SBIR Phase I:  Innovative actuating smart implant device of Transverse Tibial Transport technology for the treatment of Diabetic Foot Ulcers
awd_abstract_narration:
The broader impact/commercial potential of this Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase I project is a novel implantable therapy paradigm for initiating autologous healing in patients suffering from Diabetic Foot Ulcers (DFUs). Severe DFU’s can result in amputations, resulting in loss of limb and subsequent decline in their quality of life. The novel proposed treatment paradigm of Transverse Tibia Transport (TTT) aims to stimulate soft tissue growth to offer a new treatment paradigm to current topical or pharmacological treatments. The system stimulates patients' regenerative mechanisms needed based on mechanical forces to cause neovascularization and circulation restoration to the diseased limb to heal the ulcer. This system aims to provide an invasive therapy option for approximately 967k US patients suffering from DFU equating to a total addressable market opportunity of $8Billion.  If successful, the system will be used to treat patients with persistent DFU’s, with the future potential of expanding indications to treat less severe DFUs, other ischemic limb diseases, pressure sores and other common non-healing wounds. 

  

This Small Business Innovation Research Phase I project proposes a novel implantable system which leverages distraction osteogenesis as a treatment for diabetic foot ulcers. The objectives of this Phase 1 project are to complete the design and development of a low profile implantable Transverse Tibial Transport device integrating an active mechanical mechanism that is to transversely distract or retract a cut tibia bone segment in a programmable manner. The system will be driven using a novel mechanical actuation system that drives the TTT mechanism using a wireless controller. The first phase will be the feasibility development and testing of the distraction screw mechanism of the TTT implant device and the second phase is the feasibility development and testing of the actuation hardware platform for the implanted system. Upon completion, the system will be tested using standard mechanical failure measures suitable for commencing future preclinical validation and human use.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Summary

BioDynamik, Inc. completed Phase I feasibility for the IT3 System—a fully internal, non-invasively adjustable device intended to perform Transverse Tibial Transport (TTT) to restore blood flow in ischemic limbs (e.g., diabetic foot ulcers). Today, TTT is typically performed with external frames that protrude through the skin and can increase infection risk and patient burden. IT3 moves the actuation mechanism inside the tibia and actuates it wirelessly from outside the body, aiming to reduce complications while maintaining the therapeutic benefits of TTT. Phase I built and integrated all key subsystems, validated core performance in realistic prototypes, and established a clear path to productization and clinical translation.

Activities Completed

  • Implant & Mechanism Prototyping:
    We designed, fabricated, and tested an internal “distraction screw” implant that moves a small, osteotomized cortical bone window in a controlled manner. Bench testing characterized torque requirements, structural strength, and repeatability of the motion.
  • External Magnetic Controller (EMC):
    We developed a compact actuator containing a geared motor, magnetic drive, power electronics, sensing, and embedded control firmware. The EMC couples magnetically through soft tissue to turn the implant without percutaneous hardware.
  • Embedded Control & Wireless Telemetry:
    We implemented closed-loop motor control with real-time sensing (speed, current) and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication for pairing, control, and monitoring.
  • Mobile Application:
    An Android app was developed to handle pairing, parameter setting, start/stop commands, and live status (e.g., RPM, current, battery). The app provides simple, step-wise adjustment to deliver clinically relevant distraction/retraction profiles.
  • Magnetic Coupling Characterization:
    We measured torque transmission versus gap distance to emulate skin/soft-tissue thickness and verified adequate margin for typical anatomic conditions.
  • System-Level Validation in Realistic Models:
    We rehearsed the full workflow—from pilot-hole preparation and osteotomy to incision closure and external actuation—in Sawbones, porcine bone, and a cadaveric specimen. In each setting, the integrated system reliably distracted and retracted the bone window under app control. The cadaveric case presented a challenging soft-tissue thickness; the system maintained functional coupling and completed the planned motion sequence.
  • Design-for-Reliability Improvements:
    Phase I testing revealed practical refinements. For example, adding a compliant Oldham-style coupler reduced sensitivity to alignment in the drivetrain, and low-friction thrust bearings reduced actuation torque. A simple osteotomy guide improved surgical reproducibility and protected hardware during osteotomy.

Key Outcomes & Technical Merit

  • Feasibility Demonstrated: All Phase I technical objectives were met: implant mechanics, EMC performance, embedded/BLE functionality, magnetic torque transfer across clinically relevant gaps, and mobile-app control.
  • Integrated, End-to-End Operation: The complete system performed the intended motion sequence with non-invasive external actuation after skin closure in benchtop and anatomical models.
  • Translational workflow: We defined a clear surgical pathway—from planning and drilling through osteotomy, implant insertion, closure, and controlled actuation—to inform upcoming preclinical work and clinical protocol design.
  • Data-Driven Refinements: Test results directly guided mechanical, electrical, and workflow improvements that increase robustness and usability.

How the Award Benefited Our Company

  • De-risked Core Technology: NSF support enabled us to move from concept to an integrated working system, substantially reducing technical risk around magnetic coupling, internal mechanics, and wireless control—key hurdles for this surgical technology.
  • Accelerated Product Readiness: The program yielded tangible hardware/firmware/app assets and a validated workflow that we can now advance into precision-machined prototypes, verification testing, and formal usability studies.
  • Strengthened Regulatory & Clinical Path: Feasibility data and a defined surgical workflow support our planning for preclinical studies and future regulatory engagement.
  • Catalyzed Team & Partnerships: Phase I aligned engineering, clinical advisors, and manufacturing partners around clear specifications and acceptance criteria, improving execution speed and quality for Phase II.
  • Market Positioning: Demonstrating non-invasive actuation of an internal TTT device clarifies our differentiation versus external-frame approaches and informs reimbursement and commercialization narratives focused on infection risk, patient comfort, and care efficiency.

Broader Impacts

Chronic limb-threatening ischemia and diabetic foot ulcers carry high risks of hospitalization and amputation, with significant personal and economic costs. By removing external percutaneous hardware and enabling internal, controlled motion to stimulate local perfusion, the IT3 System aims to:

  • reduce infection risk and patient burden,
  • simplify aftercare and reduce ambulation,
  • support angiogenesis and wound healing, and
  • potentially lower total cost of care.

The same platform principles—internal actuator plus non-invasive magnetic actuation—may apply to other ischemic limb conditions and complex wounds where improving perfusion is beneficial.

Next Steps

With feasibility established, our Phase II plan focuses on: precision machining/tolerances for the implant and EMC, enhanced magnetic coupling for anatomical variability, comprehensive verification & validation (mechanical, electrical safety/EMI, software, cybersecurity, biocompatibility/sterilization, and usability), and preclinical studies to support subsequent clinical evaluation.
